# 303box

> 303box is a free browser-based 16-step 303 acid bassline and synchronized rhythm sequencer.

Canonical URL: https://303box.com/

## Core capabilities
- Program 16-step 303 patterns with note, octave, accent, slide, trigger, tie and rest states.
- Choose sawtooth or square waveform and shape cutoff, resonance, envelope modulation, decay and accent.
- Preview the 303 line with the Web Audio API.
- Inspect the 303 signal with a compact oscilloscope and FFT display.
- Connect supported MIDI hardware through the Web MIDI API and send note messages plus optional MIDI clock.
- Program a synchronized six-part rhythm machine: bass drum, snare drum, hand clap, tom, closed hi-hat and open hi-hat.
- Rhythm voice map: TR-909 bass drum; TR-606 snare drum; TR-606 closed/open hi-hats; hand-clap part selectable between TR-808 Clap, Noise Tom and TR-606 High Tom; tom part selectable between TR-808 Low Tom and TR-606 Low Tom.
- Only the Hand Clap and Tom rhythm parts expose voice choices; the other rhythm voices are fixed.
- Start the rhythm independently or synchronize its start to step 1 of the 303 sequencer.
- Randomize both acid and rhythm patterns.
- Mix 303 and rhythm levels independently; both default to 80%.
- Export the visible 303 pattern and rhythm pattern as JPG images.
- Store working sessions locally in the browser.

## Languages
- English
- Turkish

- Sequencer: https://303box.com/#sequencer
- Rhythm machine: https://303box.com/#drums
- Sequencer guide: https://303box.com/#guide

- FAQ: https://303box.com/#faq

## Historical coverage
The site includes a sourced 303 timeline covering Tadao Kikumoto, Phuture, DJ Pierre, Ron Hardy, A Guy Called Gerald, Hardfloor, Josh Wink and the continuing 303 hardware/software ecosystem.
